gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the '60 hours' it gave for the SteelSeries Arctis Nova 5X is the Bluetooth figure: on the 2.4 GHz dongle, which consoles use, SteelSeries rates it at 50 h and SoundGuys measured 42 h 10 min. Logitech's 50 h dongle claim for the G Pro X 2 measured 88 h 27 min at 75 dB, yet on Xbox the G Pro X 2 works only through a 3.5 mm cable.
standout_why: Compared against the cited SoundGuys roundup (updated 2026-09-09), which ChatGPT drew on. It gives the Nova 5X 'over 42 hours on 2.4GHz' with no conditions and no claimed figure to set it against. It gives no battery figure for the G Pro X 2 and calls it 'works almost everywhere', without saying Xbox is wired-only. So it has part of the battery point and none of the platform footnote. ChatGPT itself still printed 60 h for the Nova 5X. The cited GamesRadar page and the top RTINGS page returned no body text through the fetch tool, so I could not check them. Search snippets suggest GamesRadar's G Pro X 2 review notes Xbox is wired-only, which I did not open. No page puts each maker's battery claim next to the connection mode and a measured result, or puts 'works with Xbox' next to how it connects.
decides: This confirms the Nova 5X as the wireless pick for a shopper with an Xbox, because it is the only one of the three ChatGPT showed that works wirelessly on Xbox. But the page should say to expect about 42 h on the dongle, not 60 h. It also says the Nova 5X has no 3.5 mm input, so a flat battery cannot be bridged with a cable. It moves the G Pro X 2 to PC/PS5 only: on Xbox it is a $219.99 wired headset. For long sessions it outlasted its own claim (88 h 27 min against 50 h), but SoundGuys tested the two headsets at different volumes (75 dB against about 50%), so the hour figures are not a like-for-like ranking. The '7.1 surround' in the Razer BlackShark V2 X card title works only on Windows 11, so console buyers don't get it.

findings.note: SoundGuys gives the advertised 50 h for 2.4 GHz and 60 h for Bluetooth playback. ChatGPT's '60 hours' is therefore the Bluetooth figure. 42.17 h measured ÷ 50 h claimed = 84% of the 2.4 GHz claim.
